Justice Veena Birbal, President

 

 

 
 This is an appeal under
Section 15
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 (in short, "the Act") wherein challenge is made to order dated 09.07.2009 passed by the Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, New Delhi (in short, "the District Forum") in Complaint Case No. 285/2007.
Briefly the facts relevant for the disposal of present appeal are as under:
The respondent herein was the complainant before the Ld. District Forum.  A complaint under
Section 12
of the Act was filed by him alleging therein that he got a ticket booked on 19.12.2006 for journey from Kolkata to Delhi on 27.12.2006 through M/s Oswal Air Travels by Flight No.S2-303 for an amount of Rs.3,666/-.  It was alleged that when respondent/complainant reached Kolkata Airport for boarding and waited up till the schedule time of flight, the appellant/OP was informed that the flight had been cancelled and passengers were directed to make their own arrangements for their journey.  The agent of the other Airlines approached the respondent/complainant and other co-passengers and offered to travel through their respective Airlines by giving tickets at higher amount.  It was alleged that since the respondent/complainant had to attend an interview at Sri Nagar in the next morning, having no other option, the respondent/complainant travelled through Air Deccan to reach the destination.  On demand of refund money, the appellant's/OP's official informed that it would be refunded through the account of travelling agent i.e. M/s Oswal Air Travels.  The appellant/OP did not refund the amount of ticket to the respondent/complainant. The respondent/complainant alleged that the appellant/OP had committed deficiency in service within the meaning of Act and had prayed for compensation for the delay caused in the journey and for having purchased ticket at higher rate including not refunding the price of ticket.
The appellant/OP had opposed the complaint case by filing written version wherein it was alleged that flight No.S2-303 dated 27.12.2006 Kolkata Delhi Sector was cancelled as the flight S2-303 dated 26.12.2006 which departed from Kolkata on time could not land at Delhi Airport due to poor visibility and went back to Kolkata the same night, consequently the next day flight i.e. 27.12.2006 could not be scheduled as such it was cancelled due to prevailing bad weather in Delhi Sector.  It was alleged that there was no deficiency in service on the part of appellant/OP as the flight in question was cancelled due to bad weather conditions.
Both the parties led evidence by way of affidavits before the Ld. District Forum.
After hearing the Counsel for the parties, the Ld. District Forum held that the flight in question was cancelled due to bad weather conditions at Delhi and went back to Kolkata.  The Ld. District Forum held that in these circumstances, the sufferings of the respondent/complainant for failure to appear in the next day interview cannot be attributed to appellant/OP.  However, for non-refund of price of ticket to the respondent/complainant, the Ld. District Forum held that there was deficiency in service on the part of appellant/OP.  The price of ticket was Rs.3,666/-.  Accordingly the Ld. District Forum ordered as under:
"1.       OP will pay to the Complainant Rs.3666/- being the price of ticket.
2.        On account of deficiency of service, mental agony and harassment, OP will pay Rs.10,000/- to the Complainant.
3.        OP will pay Rs.5,000/- towards Cost of litigation.
This order be complied within 30 days.
Pronounced in open court on 9.7.09."
Aggrieved with the aforesaid order, present appeal is filed.
Ld. Counsel for the appellant has contended that there is no deficiency in service on the part of appellant/OP as the ticket price had already been refunded to respondent/complainant through the agent from whom the ticket was booked.  It is contended that the Ld. District Forum has not considered the  evidence led in this regard.  Ld. Counsel has relied upon Ex-OPC, a handwritten note wherein it is alleged that the amount of the ticket in question was refunded through agent.
On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the respondent/complainant has contended that when flight was cancelled, the respondent/complainant was told that price of ticket would be refunded to him through the travel agent only.  It is contended that the same was never refunded.  It is contended that Ex-OPC is not believable.  Ld. Counsel for respondent/complainant has relied upon affidavit of respondent/complainant dated 26.2.08 in this regard.
We have considered the submission made and perused Ex-OPC.  Ex-OPC is a photocopy of handwritten note wherein it is alleged that sale and refund of ticket in question has been affected through the agent in 2nd fortnight of December, 2006.  The name of the person who has allegedly written note is not given in Ex-OPC.  Further the name of agent to whom it is alleged that the amount is refunded is also not given.  No account statement is filed to substantiate that payment has been made to the agent as is alleged.  The date, as to when the alleged note is written, is also not mentioned.  Further as per alleged note, money is refunded to agent in 2nd fortnight of December, 2006.  The flight was cancelled on 27.12.06.  The exact date is not given as to when money was allegedly refunded to the agent. The alleged note lacks material particulars. The appellant ought to have given the necessary details to substantiate that the price of ticket has been refunded through the agent.  The respondent/complainant has categorically averred in the complaint that on demand, the refund was not given to him.  There is an affidavit of respondent/complainant to this effect also.  We find no reason to disbelieve the affidavit of respondent/complainant.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, no illegality or perversity is seen in the impugned order whereby the appellant has been directed to refund the price of the ticket i.e. Rs.3,666/- towards refund of ticket. The compensation and litigation cost awarded is also reasonable.
No case for interference is made out.  Appeal stands dismissed.  There is no order as to costs.
FDR, if any, deposited by the appellant be released after completing due formalities.
A copy  of  this  order  as  per  the  statutory  requirement  be forwarded to the parties free of charge and also to the concerned District  Forum.    The   record   of   the  District  Forum  be  sent

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 forthwith.  Thereafter the file be consigned to Record Room.
